A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from SoRA to SoMA. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, object-detection, spectral-analysis and subject-personalization results, including extensive appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds the PEGO/PiSSA benchmark comparison in Table 17.

M1.justification: SoRA is renamed SoMA, but minor-component SVD initialization, residual freezing, early-block freezing, annealing weight decay and inference merging remain unchanged. The added optimization formula documents existing training rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: The same segmentation datasets, weather-shift detection scenarios, ImageNet analysis and DreamBooth personalization tasks are retained. New Table 17 uses the existing GTAV-to-Cityscapes/BDD/Mapillary setting.

E2.justification: v2 adds PEGO and standalone rank-16 PiSSA comparisons in Table 17. This extends the benchmark comparator set beyond v1's existing principal-component ablation; earlier comparators remain.

E3.justification: The tqdm entries lose their multi-scale-flip testing designation in Tables 2–3 and corresponding appendix tables while retaining identical scores; this establishes a reporting revision, not rerunning. New Table 17 specifies PiSSA rank 16 and selects PEGO's best result within the cited hyperparameter space.

E4.justification: The spectral, rare-class, component, rank, module, frozen-block, backbone/head and qualitative analyses retain the same evidence. New Table 17 is an additional baseline benchmark comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions retain matched sampling seeds for the generation comparison and throughput averaging over multiple runs. v2 adds no run counts, uncertainty intervals or significance tests; the efficiency reporting simply moves to the appendix.

E6.justification: New Table 17 reports average mIoU of 66.30 for PEGO and 66.50 for PiSSA alongside the retained SoMA result of 68.27. PEGO slightly leads on BDD, 61.44 versus 61.31. Existing numerical results and qualitative examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds formal definitions of the model components and source/target datasets, together with the source-domain optimization objective in Equation 2. Table 1 also removes epsilon from its SMR denominator to agree with the existing equation. Earlier derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about preserving pretrained knowledge, strong cross-domain performance, broad compatibility and no additional inference overhead are retained. The introduction's 80.4% Cityscapes mIoU and 23.5-point detection improvement claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds the interpretation that PEGO's strict orthogonality constraints may restrict task adaptation. Appendix A.1 explains rank 8 for DINOv2-giant as protection against overfitting; that setting already appeared in v1's hyperparameter table. The limitations discussion is retained.

D1.justification: The front-page code pointer changes from DG-SoRA to SoMA. New Table 17 provides comparator rank/parameter information and PEGO's result-selection rule. Existing implementation settings, hardware information and initialization timing are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix E expands positioning against the already-cited PiSSA and PEGO, contrasting spectral-component selection, orthogonality constraints and adaptation at different model levels. The bibliography's set of works remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and method terminology change throughout, a problem-formulation paragraph and focused comparison discussion are added, and efficiency discussion moves into a dedicated appendix section. Additional headings and an acknowledgement appear, while most prose and organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 17 and relocates v1's efficiency Table 7 to appendix Table 16. Figures receive SoMA labels and small formatting adjustments, while their examples and plotted evidence remain unchanged. Tables and surrounding text are locally reflowed.

improvement.justification: New Table 17 fills a limited comparison gap with direct PEGO and standalone PiSSA results. The formal problem statement, additional rationale and correction of the inconsistent SMR denominator improve clarity. These are useful, bounded gains; the underlying method, broader evidence and limitations remain essentially unchanged.
